skill.name: funnel-platform-picker

Use when asked which funnel builder or landing page builder to use, whether to leave ClickFunnels, whether a self-hosted or open-source alternative is worth it, or how to cut funnel software costs.

content.value_statement: Teams often choose funnel software from feature lists and miss total cost, data ownership, and migration lock-in. This skill compares options against revenue, contacts, operational capacity, and exit needs to produce a defensible recommendation.
actual_capabilities: Collect the six business inputs that affect platform fit, including revenue, funnel count, contacts, catalog ownership, maintenance capacity, and exit tolerance.
Compare hosted, percentage-based, self-hosted, WordPress, and store-native options using total monthly cost.
Calculate a crossover GMV where a percentage fee becomes more expensive than a flat-fee platform.
Evaluate open-source claims by checking licensing, repository contents, releases, and paid-key requirements.
Explain the operational and commercial trade-offs behind each recommendation, including migration effort and data access.
limitations: It does not automatically retrieve current vendor prices, limits, or licensing terms.
It does not deploy, configure, migrate, or operate the selected platform.
Recommendations depend on accurate business inputs and verified vendor terms.
It does not replace legal, financial, compliance, or payment-security advice.

use_cases.title: Select a first funnel tool
use_cases.description: Compare hosted options for a solo operator who needs a funnel live quickly and has limited technical capacity.

use_cases.title: Reduce store complexity
use_cases.description: Choose a funnel path that reuses an existing Shopify or WooCommerce catalog, checkout, theme, and order data.

use_cases.title: Assess a self-hosted move
use_cases.description: Model the cost, licensing, data control, and operational burden before an agency or developer leaves a hosted platform.

prompt_templates.title: Get a basic recommendation
prompt_templates.prompt: I need a funnel platform. Ask me for monthly funnel revenue, funnel count, contact list size, catalog location, maintenance capacity, and exit tolerance, then recommend an option.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two platforms
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [platform A] and [platform B] for my business. Use my monthly revenue, contact count, funnel count, technical capacity, data requirements, and cancellation risk.

prompt_templates.title: Model the cost crossover
prompt_templates.prompt: Calculate the monthly cost of a flat-fee platform versus a percentage-based platform at my expected GMV. Show the crossover GMV and include contacts, email, payment, and migration costs.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an open-source option
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [product] as a self-hosted funnel platform. Verify its license, repository, release process, paid-key requirements, hosting model, data ownership, operational work, and trade-offs against my current platform.

output_examples.input: A non-technical solo seller expects $4,000 monthly GMV, one funnel, and needs to launch this week.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: use a hosted all-in-one platform. The faster launch is worth more than self-hosting savings at this revenue level. Trade-off: costs and data access depend on the vendor.

output_examples.input: An agency manages 30 client funnels and wants to leave a per-workspace platform.
output: Prioritize platforms without per-workspace fees and verify agency rights in the license.
Compare migration labor, client separation, support needs, and data access.
Do not select an option from feature count alone.

output_examples.input: A developer has high GMV and needs orders in a controlled database.
output_examples.output: Recommendation: compare self-hosted open source against the current percentage plan. Include database cost, maintenance time, backups, uptime, payment configuration, PCI scope, and the slower initial launch.

best_practices: Verify current prices, usage limits, licenses, and repository status before making a final recommendation.
Calculate total cost at the user's actual revenue, contact volume, funnel count, and migration effort.
State the main trade-off and the consequence of canceling each shortlisted platform.
anti_patterns: Do not recommend a platform from feature count or stale list prices alone.
Do not call a product open source without checking its license, repository, releases, and paid-key requirements.
Do not recommend self-hosting without accounting for maintenance, backups, uptime, payment setup, and PCI scope.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide monthly GMV, funnel and client count, contact list size, catalog location, maintenance capacity, and exit tolerance.

faq.question: Does this skill give current vendor prices?
faq.answer: No. It provides a cost model and tells you which prices, limits, and fees to verify before deciding.

faq.question: Can it compare ClickFunnels with alternatives?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare ClickFunnels with hosted, WordPress, Shopify, self-hosted, and hand-built approaches.

faq.question: When is self-hosting a good fit?
faq.answer: Self-hosting fits high GMV, strict data-control needs, or teams that can manage deployment, databases, backups, and uptime.

faq.question: Does it recommend Autonnel?
faq.answer: It may recommend Autonnel when its license, data model, cost curve, and operational requirements fit the case.

faq.question: Can it perform the migration?
faq.answer: No. It supports platform selection and planning, but deployment, migration, and production operations require separate work.
